title: Template: when is BFS the right tool?

config.prompt: Which of these problems is BFS a good fit for?

options.label: Finding the route from the Admin block to the Green that uses the fewest walkways.
Sorting a list of test marks from highest to lowest.
Adding up the marks in a list.

solution.explanation: Correct. BFS visits the vertices closest to the start first, so it finds the route with the fewest walkways. Next, try tracing it on the campus graph.

feedback.b: Not quite. Sorting a list is a job for a sorting algorithm, and a list has no edges to follow. BFS traverses a graph. Look for the option that has vertices joined by edges.
feedback.c: Not quite. Adding up a list needs one loop, not a graph. BFS traverses a graph by following its edges. Look for the option that has vertices joined by edges.

hints.body: BFS is a graph traversal. Which option is about a graph?
Buildings joined by walkways are a graph. BFS visits the vertices closest to the start first.
Two of the options are about a list of numbers, and a list has no edges to follow.
Answer: a, the route with the fewest walkways. BFS visits the buildings one walkway away first, then two walkways away, so it finds the shortest route first.
